Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Zeke Johnson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending April 30, 1940.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The only operative command of EO 8096 is its operative paragraph, which exempts William C. Shambaugh from compulsory retirement for age "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1940". The recital states the President's judgment that the public interest requires exempting William C. Shambaugh, who, during the month of August, 1939, "will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service". The command is a time-limited permission for one named employee, so it ended by its own terms on August 31, 1940; that date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day), and the exclusive reading, under which it ends as that day begins, is the alternative a reviewer should see. EO 8414 (dated May 18, 1940 in its text) recites this order by number and further exempts the same employee "for a period of one year ending August 31, 1941"; it is recorded as a later event (a separate later exemption, an extension), not as the end of this order's command, which ended by its own stated period.
